name: Trendione

lead: Trendione (Trenavar) is a metabolite of trenbolone that has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement. People use it for more muscle and a harder look.

It is inactive itself in receptor assays, with more than 100-fold lower affinity than trenbolone for androgen and progesterone receptors; the idea is that the body converts it to trenbolone. Most published work on it concerns environmental fate, since trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant and trendione is excreted in manure. No human studies exist.

paras: It has been sold as an oral supplement through online channels. No standard routine or timeline is documented.
No human safety data exist. It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014, so legal restrictions apply there.

angle.text: Trendione is sold as a trenbolone-type prohormone for more muscle and a harder look, on the idea that the body converts it to trenbolone and activates androgen receptors. It has been studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental work, not in people.

lead: Trendione (estra-4,9,11-triene-3,17-dione; code RU-2065; nicknamed 'Trenavar' or 'Trenevar') is a steroid that is a metabolite of the anabolic steroid trenbolone and has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement. Users who take prohormones of this type aim for a leaner, more muscular physique, and one T Nation member described a 'shredded' look after using it.[1][2]

The proposed chain is that the body converts a precursor into the active steroid, in the way androstenedione relates to testosterone; Wikipedia draws this comparison.[1] In receptor assays trendione itself binds androgen and progesterone receptors more than 100-fold less strongly than trenbolone.[1][3]

Most published work on it concerns environmental fate: trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant, and trendione is excreted in manure and studied in soil and runoff.[4][5] It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.[1] No human trials of trendione have been published.
infobox: Listed in the 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act[1]

paras: Wikipedia classes trendione as an androgen, anabolic steroid and progestogen prohormone and describes it as inactive itself, with affinity for the androgen and progesterone receptors more than 100-fold lower than trenbolone.[1] A receptor study found the affinity of the major trenbolone metabolites, including trendione, was under 5 percent of that of 17beta-trenbolone.[3]

Wikipedia describes it as a designer steroid sold online as a dietary supplement.[1] On T Nation, a poster listing past anabolic use said low-dose 'trenevar' in 2015 helped them get very lean.[2] Another thread asks how long trendione and related products remain traceable in the body.[6]
The same Wikipedia article cites a 2016 Military Medicine case report of acute pancreatitis linked to a supplement containing anabolic-androgenic steroids.[1]
Trendione is named in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.[1]

Studies of cattle implanted with trenbolone acetate identify 17alpha-trenbolone and trendione as main metabolites in manure. Research has examined how they degrade in agricultural soils, sorb to soil and break down under light.[4][5]
No studies found. Published work is limited to laboratory receptor assays and environmental studies.

lore.intro: On T Nation, trendione appears in threads on prohormones, recomposition and drug-test detection windows.[2][6]
